main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling devil curry in the shared kitchen without the smell disturbing A's work calls, B's room and clothes, and C's laundry.

A-B.evidence: A opposed strong-smelling cooking (T1) and B shared the complaint (T2). Both ended up accepting D's arrangement (T7 'That works for me', T14 'Okay, thanks. That works'), but they never addressed each other.

A-C.evidence: Both complained about the smell (T1, T3). A accepted cooking after 7 (T7) and C accepted cooking on non-laundry days (T22). They never spoke to each other.

A-D.evidence: A asked that nobody cook smelly food (initial); D said 'it's what I cook' (T4). A then asked for after 7 or Saturday (T5), D agreed (T6), and A said 'That works for me' (T7). D later moved to Tue/Thu/Sat/Sun (T18).

B-C.evidence: Both said D's after-7 plan doesn't fix the problem (T8, T9). They ended with compatible accepted conditions (T14, T22), but never addressed each other.

B-D.evidence: B rejected the after-7 plan (T8). B proposed the window and yard door plan with advance notice (T12), D agreed to it (T13), and B said 'That works' (T14).

C-D.evidence: C rejected the plan (T9, T15) and proposed cooking on non-laundry days (T17). D accepted: 'Tuesdays, Thursdays, Saturdays, or Sundays. That works for me' (T18). C replied 'That works' (T22).
